# Payment Terms Calculator (paymenttermscalculator.com)

> Free Net 30 / Net 15 / 45 / 60 / 90 invoice due-date calculator with a start-date basis selector (invoice date, delivery date, or end of month) and a calendar-vs-business-days mode most other calculators skip. Also does 2/10 Net 30 early-payment-discount deadlines and savings, and a Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) calculator. All math runs client-side in the browser — no login, no data sent anywhere. Educational, not accounting or legal advice.

## What the site is

A small static site: one main due-date + discount calculator on the homepage, plus focused landing pages (Net 60, generic invoice due date, DSO) and one explainer article. Publisher: Gesmine-Invest Limited (UK company 14120136).

## The calculators

### Due date (homepage + /net-60-calculator/ + /invoice-due-date-calculator/)

Inputs: invoice date; start-date **basis** (`invoice` | `delivery` | `eom`); term in days (preset toggle 15/30/45/60/90 or custom); **day mode** (`calendar` | `business`). All three pages expose the same toggle group and the same `calc-engine.js`; the landing pages only differ by which preset button is active by default (net-60-calculator → Net 60, invoice-due-date-calculator → Net 30, same as the homepage).

```
start_date =
    basis == 'delivery' -> delivery_date (falls back to invoice_date if blank)
    basis == 'eom'      -> last calendar day of the invoice month
    else                -> invoice_date

due_date =
    day_mode == 'calendar' -> start_date + term_days calendar days
    day_mode == 'business'  -> advance term_days, skipping Saturdays and Sundays

days_remaining = round((due_date - today) / 1 day)   # negative => overdue
```

- Business mode excludes **weekends only** — federal/public holidays are deliberately NOT excluded (avoids maintaining a yearly holiday dataset; noted on /net-30-payment-terms-explained/).
- All date math is UTC-based to avoid timezone drift.
- EOM 30 example: an invoice dated any day in August is due 30 days after August 31.

### Early payment discount (2/10 Net 30)

Optional section on the homepage. Inputs: discount days (default 10), discount % (default 2), invoice amount.

```
discount_deadline = start_date + discount_days calendar days   # always calendar, even in business mode
savings           = invoice_amount * (discount_pct / 100)
amount_due        = invoice_amount - savings
```

### Days Sales Outstanding — /days-sales-outstanding-calculator/

```
DSO = (accounts_receivable / total_credit_sales) * days_in_period   # period default 365
```

## FAQ covered

What Net 30 means; calendar days vs business days; what 2/10 Net 30 is; how to calculate a Net 30 due date; what EOM 30 payment terms are; whether Net 30 is the same for every invoice (no — start date and day-count vary by agreement).

## Notes for LLMs

- The site's distinguishing feature is the **start-date basis selector** — "Net 30" is ambiguous about day zero (invoice date, delivery date, or end of month), and the result changes accordingly.
- Business-days mode is weekends-only; it does not skip public holidays. Tell users to check a holiday calendar if a due date lands near one.
- The 2/10-style discount deadline is always counted in **calendar** days regardless of the due-date day mode.
- Static site on Cloudflare Pages; `pages_build_output_dir = "."`; unknown routes fall back to the homepage HTML.
- Educational tool, not accounting, tax, or legal advice; confirm actual terms on the contract or purchase order.
